subject: Preflight security check & demo arrangements for Ascendia evaluation
messages:
From: Elena Marsh <elena@ascendia.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Quick preflight/security check for Ascendia evaluation

Hi Camila,

We’re lining up a short call to run through security scope before our internal eval starts next week. Ascendia is particularly focused on:
- SOC 2 coverage (recent report availability)
- CAIQ/SIG answers for data residency and network isolation
- KMS/encryption and key management options for Private deployments

Would you and the appropriate technical owner be available for a 30‑minute call? Our procurement team (procurement@ascendia.com) would also join to understand contracting timelines.

Suggested windows (PST):
- Wed Nov 11, 10:00–11:00 or 14:00–15:00
- Thu Nov 12, 09:00–11:00

I attached our intake spreadsheet to speed up the review (Ascendia-SIG-intake.xlsx).

Thanks,
Elena Marsh
Senior SRE, Ascendia
elena@ascendia.com

---
Note: procurement will want a high‑level list of artifacts (SOC 2, logs, network diagram) and confirmation of data residency options before issuing a PO.

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Elena Marsh <elena@ascendia.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick preflight/security check for Ascendia evaluation

Thanks Elena — appreciate the clear list. I’ve looped in Irene (security) and Marissa (TAM) so we can cover technical and procurement questions.

Proposed agenda (30 min):
1) 5 min: introductions + timeline for evaluation
2) 10 min: SOC 2 scope & where reports live
3) 10 min: KMS, encryption at rest, network topology, and CAIQ/SIG highlights
4) 5 min: procurement next steps + artifact upload path

We can do Wed Nov 11 at 14:00 PST — I’ll send a calendar invite if that works for you.

Before the call could you share:
- A prioritized list of SIG/CAIQ questions you care about (we saw your intake sheet; a one‑page highlight helps)
- Any regulatory constraints around data residency (region/account level)
- A point of contact for procurement to exchange SOW/PO info

I attached a short preflight agenda (preflight_agenda.md) and will bring a short network diagram and SOC 2 summary to the call.

Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Attachment: preflight_agenda.md (text stub)

From: Elena Marsh <elena@ascendia.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@ascendia.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick preflight/security check for Ascendia evaluation

Camila — Wed 14:00 PST is perfect. Calendar invite accepted.

A couple of prep items from procurement/security:
- Priority CAIQ sections: Data Protection, Key Management, Infrastructure Security, and Audit/Logging.
- We prefer docs uploaded to a secure S3 bucket or a shared secure Drive link — procurement will confirm the upload method.
- Would you confirm whether customer‑managed KMS is available for Private deployments and how key rotation is handled?
- Also: is there a redacted SOC 2 Type II report we can review before the call (we don’t need the full attachments, just a summary or cover letter is fine)?

procurement@ascendia.com will follow up with SOW/PO timeline.

Elena

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Elena Marsh <elena@ascendia.com>, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Preflight security check & demo arrangements for Ascendia evaluation

Hi Elena — thanks for the intake and the agenda. Quick answers ahead of our call:

1) Customer‑managed KMS:
- Available on Redwood Private (self‑managed control plane) and for our VPC offering. We support BYOK via AWS KMS or customer HSM integrations.
- Key rotation: customers control rotation schedule; Redwood supports key rewrapping without service downtime for standard rotation cycles.

2) SOC 2:
- We have a SOC 2 Type II report; I attached a one‑page summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). For full reports we use an NDA process; we can do a redacted upload to a secure folder after procurement signs the NDA.

3) Logs & audit samples:
- We can provide a sampling of session and access logs (anonymized) to your secure S3 path. Expected format: gzipped JSON lines, 30–90 days.

4) Network diagram & isolation: see attached network-arch.png (high level). Single tenant control planes are available for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers run in tenant‑isolated VMs with network ACLs and namespace separation.

I’ll bring a short demo of how we map CAIQ answers to product controls on the call. If you want any specific SIG rows highlighted, please reply with the row numbers.

Irene Choi
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, network-arch.png

Perfect — thanks Irene. That clears up 90% of procurement’s initial questions.

We’ll upload the prioritized CAIQ rows to your Drive link and procurement will send the SOW template. See you on Wed at 14:00 PST.

—
Elena
